Mark Aitken has signed with the Colorado Rockies, one year for $21 million. The Angels were the team with the reported interest in C116, the A's were the team with the history, and Colorado is the team that closed. The money is almost exactly what he made in 2041, $21.4M, so this was never about Aitken being priced as a player in decline. He is coming off a .283 season with 153 hits, 33 homeruns, 87 RBI and 3.2 WAR in 540 at bats, a 93 overall first baseman with 3 Gold Gloves and the 2037 Playoff MVP, and he homered in the World Series that clinched the seventh title. The length is the detail that will be argued over. One year is a short commitment for a player at the top of the market, and it puts Aitken back in free agency after 2042. Whether that reads as a door left open or simply the deal that was there, he has not said. What it leaves behind in Oakland is bigger than a lineup spot. Aitken is an Oakland native who grew up swinging a bat in East Oakland. He owns his place in Jack London, where he lives with his wife and three kids. He has been the A's player rep and community liaison, and he runs Aitken Little Leaguers, free baseball for East Oakland kids heading into its sixth year. He showed up at city council and planning hearings, brought Benji Dillon to the DEIR session, was a major voice in the Baylight negotiations, and was the veteran who reached out to Kevin Clark the day Clark was called up. In C114 he wrote that "the number on the calendar means more than the number on my back," and that "the city has a way of holding on to its own, and I've been its own for a long, long time." This time the city did not hold on. For the A's, the move this page laid out in C116 now happens: Ernesto Quintero slides across the diamond to first base. That opens third base outright to the bat-or-glove contest between Kevin Clark, .327 in 55 at bats with 83 discipline and 87 clutch, and Giancarlo Hernandez, the 96 fielding glove from the Carmen Mesa trade. It also comes in the same off-season Vinnie Keane retired, which means the A's go into 2042 without the two longest-standing local voices in their clubhouse. Word around the league is that the Anaheim Angels have strong interest in Mark Aitken, the A's first baseman and one of the top free agents on the market at 93 overall. Aitken was born in California, and a contender in Anaheim could sell him a short drive and a starting job. But Aitken is an Oakland native, and his whole life is here. He owns his place in Jack London, where he lives with his wife and three kids. He is the A's player rep and community liaison, he runs Aitken Little Leaguers, free baseball for East Oakland kids now going into its sixth year, and he shows up at city council and planning hearings without ever testifying, the way he brought Benji Dillon to the DEIR session.
